# BEEBEEB DESKTOP: THIRD-PARTY LICENCES AND SOURCE OFFER

Beebeeb 0.9.0 (Initlabs B.V.). This file lists the software and data that is part of the Beebeeb desktop
app (beebeeb-desktop.exe) and its two helper programs (beebeeb-office-render.exe, beebeeb-media-helper.exe),
with each one's licence. It is installed beside the app and opened from Settings > About > Open-source licences.

Generated by packaging/licences/generate.sh (cargo-about); do not edit by hand.

## 3. DATA COMPILED INTO THE PDF RENDERER, AND OTHER NOTICES

# Third-party notices: bundled data

Data that is compiled into the app through the PDF renderer (`hayro`, Apache-2.0 OR MIT) and whose licence asks
that its notice goes with a binary. The installer ships it: `packaging/licences/generate.sh` copies this file into
`THIRD-PARTY-LICENSES.md` (section 3), which sits beside the exes and opens from Settings > About > Open-source
licences. Edit this file, then run that script (its `--check` and `packaging/licences/check.py` fail on a stale copy).

Also compiled in, with nothing asked of a binary: two colour profiles in `hayro-interpret`
(`CGATS001Compat-v2-micro.icc` and `LAB.icc`, both CC0-1.0 by that crate's `assets/README.md`).


### The audio decoders (`symphonia`, MPL-2.0), in the Office editor's helper

`deckcraft-engine` (the slide editor's engine, held in `beebeeb-io/desktop-office`) brings the `symphonia` family
(`symphonia`, `symphonia-core`, `symphonia-metadata`, `symphonia-utils-xiph`, `symphonia-bundle-flac`, `symphonia-bundle-mp3`,
`symphonia-codec-alac`, `symphonia-codec-pcm`, `symphonia-codec-vorbis`, `symphonia-format-isomp4`, `symphonia-format-ogg`
and `symphonia-format-riff`, version 0.5.5): MPL-2.0, used unmodified, accepted for the editor on 2026-11-18. Their
source links are in section 4 of `THIRD-PARTY-LICENSES.md`, which `packaging/licences/generate.sh` writes from the lock
files, and the licence text is in its section 5.


### Ubuntu Light, in the Office viewer's helper

Ubuntu Light (`Ubuntu-Light.ttf`, Dalton Maag Ltd for Canonical, via `epaint_default_fonts` 0.37), the Office engine's last-resort text face, compiled into `beebeeb-office-render`: Ubuntu Font Licence 1.0 (`Ubuntu-font-1.0`), its notice and licence carried in the font's own metadata. The licence text is `packaging/licences/texts/UFL-1.0.txt` (from `epaint_default_fonts`), and goes into the shipped notice's section 2.

### Lucide and Feather icons in the Beebeeb app

The file and folder icons in the Drive app's file lists, grids and sidebar (`native/beebeeb-drive-rune/src/theme/file_icon_art.rs`)
are path data from Lucide release 1.77.0 (github.com/lucide-icons/lucide, tag `1.77.0`, `icons/<name>.svg`), re-stroked
to the app's line width and, for folders, combined with a second Lucide icon as the emblem. The app's other line glyphs
(the board, toolbar and settings icons) are path data from Feather (github.com/feathericons/feather) or drawn after it.
Lucide is ISC; the icons Lucide derives from Feather, and the Feather glyphs themselves, are MIT. Lucide's licence, verbatim
from its `LICENSE` at tag `1.77.0`:

```

//! EdDSA Signatures.

use super::ops::ELEM_LEN;
use crate::digest;

pub mod signing;
pub mod verification;

/// The length of an Ed25519 public key.
pub const ED25519_PUBLIC_KEY_LEN: usize = ELEM_LEN;

pub fn eddsa_digest(signature_r: &[u8], public_key: &[u8], msg: &[u8]) -> digest::Digest {
    let mut ctx = digest::Context::new(&digest::SHA512);
    ctx.update(signature_r);
    ctx.update(public_key);
    ctx.update(msg);
    ctx.finish()
}

use crate::limb::Limb;

#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
#[repr(transparent)]
pub struct N0([Limb; 2]);

impl N0 {
    #[cfg(feature = "alloc")]
    pub(super) const LIMBS_USED: usize = 64 / crate::limb::LIMB_BITS;

    #[inline]
    pub const fn precalculated(n0: u64) -> Self {
        #[cfg(target_pointer_width = "64")]
        {
            Self([n0, 0])
        }

        #[cfg(target_pointer_width = "32")]
        {
            Self([n0 as Limb, (n0 >> crate::limb::LIMB_BITS) as Limb])
        }
    }
}

}

    fn from(source: KeyRejected) -> Self {
        super::erase(source)
    }
}

// SPECIAL, DIRECT, INDIRECT, OR CONSEQUENTIAL DAMAGES OR ANY DAMAGES
// WHATSOEVER RESULTING FROM LOSS OF USE, DATA OR PROFITS, WHETHER IN AN ACTION
// OF CONTRACT, NEGLIGENCE OR OTHER TORTIOUS ACTION, ARISING OUT OF OR IN
// CONNECTION WITH THE USE OR PERFORMANCE OF THIS SOFTWARE.

#[cfg(target_arch = "x86")]
pub fn shift_full_blocks<const BLOCK_LEN: usize>(
    in_out: super::overlapping::Overlapping<'_, u8>,
    mut transform: impl FnMut(&[u8; BLOCK_LEN]) -> [u8; BLOCK_LEN],
) {
    let (in_out, src) = in_out.into_slice_src_mut();
    let in_out_len = in_out[src.clone()].len();

    for i in (0..in_out_len).step_by(BLOCK_LEN) {
        let block = {
            let input =
                <&[u8; BLOCK_LEN]>::try_from(&in_out[(src.start + i)..][..BLOCK_LEN]).unwrap();
            transform(input)
        };
        let output = <&mut [u8; BLOCK_LEN]>::try_from(&mut in_out[i..][..BLOCK_LEN]).unwrap();
        *output = block;
    }
}
```

/// Polyfill for `Option::unwrap()` as a const fn; feature `const_option`.
/// https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/67441.
/// TODO(MSRV): Replace this with `x.unwrap()`.
///
/// `T: Copy` avoids "constant functions cannot evaluate destructors."
pub const fn unwrap_const<T>(x: Option<T>) -> T
where
    T: Copy,
{
    if let Some(x) = x {
        x
    } else {
        panic!("unwrap_const on `None`");
    }
}

//! Utilities to make dealing with slices less tediuous.

/// Replaces the first N elements of `a` with the first N elements of `b`, where
/// N is `core::cmp::min(a.len(), b.len())`, leaving the rest unchanged.
pub fn overwrite_at_start<T: Copy>(a: &mut [T], b: &[T]) {
    a.iter_mut().zip(b).for_each(|(a, b)| {
        *a = *b;
    });
}
```

#include <stdint.h>

#if HAVE_CONFIG_H
# include "config.h"
#endif

#define PROTO_RETURN size_t
#define PROTO_ARGS                              \
        const uint8_t low[16],                  \
        const uint8_t high[16],                 \
        const uint8_t *restrict const in,       \
        uint8_t *restrict const out,            \
        const size_t len
#define PROTO(name)                     \
        PROTO_RETURN                    \
        name (PROTO_ARGS)

PROTO(reedsolomon_gal_mul);
PROTO(reedsolomon_gal_mul_xor);

typedef enum {
        REEDSOLOMON_CPU_GENERIC = 0,
        REEDSOLOMON_CPU_SSE2 = 1,
        REEDSOLOMON_CPU_SSSE3 = 2,
        REEDSOLOMON_CPU_AVX = 3,
        REEDSOLOMON_CPU_AVX2 = 4,
        REEDSOLOMON_CPU_NEON = 5,
        REEDSOLOMON_CPU_ALTIVEC = 6,
} reedsolomon_cpu_support;

reedsolomon_cpu_support reedsolomon_determine_cpu_support(void);
```

are permissively licensed (MIT/Apache-2.0/BSD/ISC/Zlib) and fetched through crates.io or pinned Git sources.
The craft-pdf writer and Krilla 0.8.2 backend are pinned to storytold/craft-libs revision
b926b5c03e256c86ca10934f58d03f628810b5b7. The backend retains its MIT OR Apache-2.0 licensing
and upstream bundled material; see that revision's licenses/pdf-writer/ and ATTRIBUTION.md.
The backend patch prevents finalization during an unwind and rejects a writer after failed
cleanup. WordCraft enables only writing; PDF import and its image decoders are not enabled.

No Microsoft, Adobe, Avid or Autodesk icons, images, templates or artwork are included.

Bundled egui font icons

The canonical egui0.37 dependency includes egui-icons.ttf (a small subset of emoji-icon-font)
through default_fonts, and emoji-icon-font.ttf through monochrome_emoji_fonts. Both are embedded
by the UI font definitions. Their upstream project is https://github.com/jslegers/emoji-icon-font;
the exact copyright and permission notice from the pinned egui dependency follows.
